note: Story video for Dispatch No. 025, drawn only from the verified captions of Nos. 025 and 026. Photos: Clifford K. Berryman cartoon "Waiting for his number!", 29 October 1940, NARA 6012221, unrestricted; President Roosevelt signs the Selective Training and Service Act, 16 September 1940, public domain (Wikimedia Commons, SelectiveServiceActRoosevelt.jpg); Secretary of War Newton D. Baker draws the first number of the 1917 draft lottery, 20 July 1917, War Department, public domain (Wikimedia Commons, U.S._draft_lottery.jpg), shown where the script says the 1940 bowl was last used for the First World War draft; Secretary of War Henry L. No public domain film of the 1940 drawing is online: Universal Newsreel vol. 12 release 924 (NARA 234272595) has it but NARA flags possible copyright, so this is a Story Card.

segments.say: A blindfolded man reached into a giant glass bowl, and millions of young American men waited to hear their number.
segments.caption: A blindfolded man reached into a giant glass bowl, and millions of young American men waited to hear their number.

segments.say: October twenty ninth, nineteen forty. Washington draws the lottery for America's first peacetime draft.
segments.caption: 29 October 1940. Washington draws the lottery for America's first peacetime draft.

segments.say: President Roosevelt had signed the Selective Training and Service Act on September sixteenth.
segments.caption: President Roosevelt had signed the Selective Training and Service Act on 16 September.

segments.say: Men from twenty one to thirty five had registered two weeks before. Every one of them had a number.
segments.caption: Men from 21 to 35 had registered two weeks before. Every one of them had a number.

segments.say: The order they would be called in came out of a bowl last used for the draft of the First World War.
segments.caption: The order they would be called in came out of a bowl last used for the draft of the First World War.

segments.say: Secretary of War Henry Stimson, blindfolded, pulled out the first capsule.
segments.caption: Secretary of War Henry Stimson, blindfolded, pulled out the first capsule.

segments.say: President Roosevelt red the number aloud. One fifty eight.
segments.caption: President Roosevelt read the number aloud: 158.

segments.say: Six thousand, one hundred seventy five men across America held that number.
segments.caption: 6,175 men across America held that number.

segments.say: Cartoonist Clifford Berryman drew the scene that day, with Mars, the god of war, at the bowl, and Uncle Sam waiting his turn.
segments.caption: Cartoonist Clifford Berryman drew the scene that day, with Mars, the god of war, at the bowl and Uncle Sam waiting his turn.

segments.say: The men called that winter expected to serve one year. Thirteen months later came Pearl Harbor.
segments.caption: The men called that winter expected to serve one year. Thirteen months later came Pearl Harbor.
